stem: A client has persistent fatigue, easy bruising or bleeding, frequent infections, bone pain, and abnormal blood counts. The peripheral blood smear also shows immature blast cells. Which disorder requires prompt hematologic evaluation?
rationale: NCI describes acute leukemias as bone-marrow malignancies involving excessive abnormal immature blood cells and notes that they can disrupt normal red cells, white cells, and platelets. Compatible manifestations include fatigue or weakness, infection or fever, easy bruising or bleeding, and bone or joint pain. The added finding of circulating blast cells makes acute leukemia the best answer. Iron-deficiency anemia does not explain blasts, immune thrombocytopenia does not explain the full multi-line and blast pattern, and degenerative joint disease does not explain the hematologic findings.
educational_objective: Recognize a pattern of fatigue, infection, bruising or bleeding, bone pain, abnormal blood counts, and circulating blasts as concerning for acute leukemia and requiring prompt hematologic evaluation.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Treatment (PDQ®) — Patient Version; SEER Training Modules — Physical Exam
source_version_date: Current NCI PDQ rechecked 2026-08-17; SEER Physical Exam page updated 2025-12-02

source_claim_supported: Acute leukemia can involve abnormal immature blast cells and disrupt normal hematopoiesis, producing fatigue, infection, bruising or bleeding, and bone/joint pain; blood and bone marrow testing are used for diagnosis.

correction_summary: Strengthened the original nonspecific symptom cluster by adding the source-supported finding of circulating immature blast cells, which removes second-answer ambiguity from other cytopenic disorders. Updated the exact SEER page currentness to its 2025-12-02 revision and used current NCI acute-leukemia PDQ content. Correct answer remains C; difficulty reduced from hard to moderate.
